sets.title: can / can't for what is possible and wh- questions with can
sets.intro: Use can and can't to say what is possible or allowed in a place. For questions, put the question word first and can before the subject.

watch.why: Can never takes -s.
In questions, can goes before the subject.

watch.wrong: You can to see the castle.
watch.why: After can we use the base verb, without to.

sets.title: Explaining words and writing lists
sets.intro: When you don't know a word, explain it with a kind of, like, or kind of like. In lists of three or more things, use commas and put and before the last one.

watch.wrong: It's kind like a small bus.

sets.title: Simple past: regular and irregular verbs
sets.intro: Use the simple past for finished actions. Regular verbs end in -ed. Irregular verbs change: go becomes went, buy becomes bought. The form is the same for all people.

watch.why: Buy is irregular: its past form is bought.
With consonant + y, change y to i and add -ed.
Go is irregular: went.
